implemented_requirements.evidence: Game2048.SIZE = 4 and grid created with [[0] * self.SIZE for _ in range(self.SIZE)]
GameGUI._bind_keys binds <Left>, <Right>, <Up>, <Down> to handle_move which calls Game2048.move

implemented_requirements.requirement: Sliding and merging of equal tiles
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game2048._slide_row implements slide‑and‑merge logic; Game2048._move applies it to rows/columns

implemented_requirements.requirement: New random tile after each successful move
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game2048.move calls add_random_tile() after a successful _move

implemented_requirements.requirement: Random tile is 2 (90%) or 4 (10%) placed in an empty cell
implemented_requirements.evidence: add_random_tile selects a random empty cell and sets value 2 if random()<0.9 else 4

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game‑over detection when no moves are possible
implemented_requirements.evidence: After each move, Game2048.move checks can_move(); if false, sets self.over = True
Game2048.score is increased by the sum of merged values; displayed via score_var in GUI
Game2048.highest updated after each move and after reset; displayed via highest_var in GUI

implemented_requirements.requirement: Display of score and highest tile
implemented_requirements.evidence: GUI creates labels bound to score_var and highest_var and updates them in refresh()
GameGUI.new_game calls Game2048.reset() and refreshes the UI

judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable implementation of the classic 2048 game. Core mechanics, arrow‑key controls, random tile spawning, score/highest‑tile tracking, and game‑over detection are all present and wired to a Tkinter UI. No missing or placeholder code is observed, making the solution functionally complete and highly likely to execute successfully.
